function: CNN estimates the composite direct plus RIS-reflected uplink channel from received pilot subblocks, outputting the real and imaginary channel parts (p. 1, 3-4).
system: Uplink: M=30-antenna BS, K=6-antenna UE, passive reflecting RIS with N=30 elements, block flat fading, Tp=192 pilots; band not stated, footnote cites sub-6 GHz scattering (p. 2, 4).
method: Supervised CNN (three conv layers, two 1024-unit dense layers, 50% dropout); input stacks real, imaginary, magnitude of received subblocks; trained on labeled channel pairs with Adam (p. 3-4).
data_channel: Own simulation: 100 Rayleigh fading realizations, SNR 0 to 20 dB, 80,000 samples, 80% training and 20% validation and testing; no standard or measured channel (p. 4-5).
test_conditions: Training and testing within SNR 0 to 20 dB, same Rayleigh model, M=30, K=6, N=30, Tp=192; remaining 20% of data used for validation and testing (p. 4-5).
baselines: Non-learned: LS and LMMSE. Learned: MLP, SRNet (ref. 6), SRDnNet (ref. 7), JDCNet (ref. 8) (p. 5).
metrics: NMSE versus SNR (0 to 20 dB), with and without direct channel; analytical complexity orders; rate and pilot analyses mentioned but omitted (p. 4-5).
complexity: Online O(L1^2 + M Tp/K) with L1=1024; about O(1e6) versus O(1e11) for LS and O(3e11) for LMMSE at N=30, K=6, Tp=192 (p. 4).
q1_support: p. 4: "100 different Raleigh fading channel realizations" - the paper's own Rayleigh simulation; no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured channel is used.
q2_support: p. 5: "Both the training and testing are performed within the aforementioned SNR range" - held-out part of the same Rayleigh data; no other scenario, antenna count, RIS size, pilot count or band is tested.
q3_support: p. 5: "compared to LS and MMSE under varying SNR conditions" (Fig. 3) and "compared with several benchmark algorithms, including MLP, SRNet [6], SRDnNet [7], and JDCNet [8]" (Fig. 4), both on NMSE.
q4_support: p. 4: "Table I summarizes the computational complexities of the LS, LMMSE, and DL-Based channel estimation methods"; the proposed method has online complexity O(L1^2 + fCNN), about O(1x10^6) against O(1x10^11) for LS.
q5_support: p. 5: "A total of 80, 000 data is generated of which 80% is used for training" - self-generated Rayleigh data (p. 4); no code or data link or DOI is given in the letter.
notes: Area 2, composite (direct plus cascaded) channel estimation. Footnote 2 on p. 2 justifies the unstructured channel model for rich-scattering sub-6 GHz systems but the simulated band is not stated. Results on rate versus SNR and pilots versus SNR are mentioned on p. 5 but omitted, so they are not counted for q2.
